regions.purpose: The full-screen map canvas — a pin for every Collection Entry in every visible Collection. Panning and zooming move the viewport; a long-press drops a pin.
Shows the settings (cog) icon and opens the Settings surface.
Shows the close (X) icon and cancels the add-to-collection flow, dropping the carried Collection and returning to CollectionDetail.

A search field across the top-center, spanning roughly 30% of the surface width so it never overlaps the navigationIcon. Tapping it widens the field and raises the keyboard. Results are biased near the current map viewport — the visible center is the query's locality anchor — and interleave two sources: Locations the user already has Entries for (rendered with their owning Collection's color dot) and unadopted provider candidates. Whether the field queries per keystroke or only on submit is a per-provider trait declared on LocationProvider (doc03.02.02); the field follows the active provider's setting. Present in all modes — finding a place is part of completing the add flow. In searchResults mode the field renders the committed query with a trailing close (X) affordance that fires CLEAR_SEARCH.
regions.rendering: The dropdown's container consumes `WindowInsets.ime` so its available height is screen − keyboard − search-field; the search-results list scrolls within that remaining height. No keyboard-height constants or platform branches — the inset animates in lockstep with the IME on show/hide.

regions.purpose: A chip overlaid on the upper-center of the map in searchResults mode, holding the *Search this area* affordance. Renders only when the live viewport has drifted past a threshold from `search-context.viewportAtQuery` (the viewport active when the current candidate set was issued). Tapping it fires SEARCH_THIS_AREA, which re-runs the committed query against the now-current viewport and replaces the candidate pins.
An extended floating action button anchored bottom-end over the map, opening the CollectionList sheet (a tall bottom-sheet drawer hosted here per doc02.04 Rule 2).

A Material 3 input/assist chip overlaid on the upper area of the map (anchored to the safe-area inset, sitting under the search field). Renders only when `filter-context` is set. Leading content reflects the filter: for a single-Collection filter, the Collection's appearance dot; for a multi-Collection filter, a stacked-dots glyph (or the leading Collection's dot). Label reads the Collection name when n=1 or `Filtered: {n} Collections` when n>1. Trailing close (X) icon fires CLEAR_FILTER. Tapping the chip body (not the close) fires TAP_FILTER_CHIP and reopens CollectionList in selection mode with the active filter pre-checked. Context-driven overlay (doc02.04 Rule 1); chrome is unchanged so this is not a mode.
A panel along the bottom of the surface naming the target Collection — "Adding to {collectionName}".

affordances.label: Clear filter
affordances.rendering: Trailing close (X) icon on the filterChip; tapping it drops `filter-context` and restores all Collections' pins.

affordances.label: Review
affordances.rendering: Material 3 Snackbar action — appears transiently after AddLocationToCollection's PICK_COLLECTION. Not a persistent region; the chrome is unchanged in browse mode.

affordances.label: Dismiss
affordances.rendering: Snackbar timeout or swipe-dismiss. Drops pending-review-context; the Entry stays saved.

affordances.label: Search
affordances.rendering: A button on the dropdown's action row — the row directly under the search field and above the hit list, shared with commit-search-to-map. Always present while the dropdown is open, irrespective of the active provider's `supportsTypeahead` trait. Tapping it re-issues the current query against the current viewport via Location.resolve; the dropdown's hit list refreshes in place and the field, keyboard, and dropdown stay open. Useful for non-typeahead providers (the user types then submits) and for typeahead providers when the viewport has moved since the last keystroke.

affordances.label: Search on map
affordances.rendering: A button on the dropdown's action row — the row directly under the search field and above the hit list, shared with submit-search. Only renders when the dropdown contains at least one unadopted provider candidate. Existing-entry-only results do not enable it (nothing new to pin). Tapping it dismisses the dropdown and keyboard, sets `search-context` from the current query / candidate set / viewport, and pivots the surface into searchResults mode.

affordances.label: Clear search
affordances.rendering: A trailing close (X) icon on the search field when search-context is set, *and* an implicit fire on the first keystroke into the field while search-context is set — editing the query is treated as starting a new search, never as filtering the committed candidate set.

shows: a pin at the Entry's Location coordinates
the pin colored by its Collection's appearance
reviewed or unreviewed styling from the Entry's Review status

a darkened color variant when the pin's Location matches the host sheet currently open over MapOverview (LocationSheet, EntrySheet, or a Peek-shaped PinSheet) — a derived projection of which sheet is active, not a separately carried context; clears on sheet dismiss. See statechart `meta.derivedRendering.selectedPin` on MapOverview (doc02.02.01)

affordance.label: Tap multi-entry pin
affordance.appliesWhen: the pin's Location is referenced by more than one Collection Entry

altAffordances.label: Tap 1-entry pin
altAffordances.appliesWhen: the pin's Location is referenced by exactly one Collection Entry

lists.emptyState: Before any Collection has Entries the map shows no pins; the collectionsButton still points the user toward creating a Collection.
lists.visibility: When `filter-context` is set, only pins whose owning Collection's id is in `filter-context.collectionIds` render; every other pin is hidden. With no `filter-context` set, every Collection's pins render.

shows: for existing-entry hits: the owning Collection's color dot (one dot per Entry referencing the Location); for candidate hits: no dot

affordance.label: Pick a provider candidate (browse mode)
affordance.appliesWhen: the hit is an unadopted provider candidate — no saved Location with this (sourceType, sourceId) — and the user is in browse mode (no `collection-context`)

altAffordances.label: Pick a provider candidate (add-to-collection mode)
altAffordances.appliesWhen: same affordance as pick-search-result, but emitted when `collection-context` is set so the candidate is funneled straight into the collection picker, skipping LocationSheet

altAffordances.label: Pick an existing entry
altAffordances.appliesWhen: the hit is an existing Location with at least one Collection Entry — LocationSheet's single-entry rendering shortcut applies downstream

lists.composition: The list is one ranked view over two upstream sources, merged at the surface and never persisted: (a) existing-entry hits derived in-memory from `all-entries` filtered by the query, biased by the live `viewport`; (b) unadopted provider candidates from the active LocationProvider's `resolve(query, near=viewport.center)` (doc03.02.02). The declared `reads: provider-results` names the async/external source; the existing-entry half rides the surface's already-loaded `all-entries` stream and needs no separate read.
lists.ordering: Hits compete on a single axis — proximity to the viewport center, with displayName match strength as the tiebreaker — not segregated into existing-vs-candidate sections. Duplicate suppression: a provider candidate whose (sourceType, sourceId) matches a saved Location via LocationRepository.findByIdentity is dropped in favor of the existing-entry hit.
lists.emptyState: An empty search field shows no results; the map stays the focus. Existing-entry matches surface as soon as the query is non-empty. Provider candidates surface per the active provider's `supportsTypeahead` trait (per keystroke when true, on submit otherwise — see doc03.02.02).

shows: a pin at the candidate's coordinates, drawn with the same teardrop body as Collection Entry pins but slightly smaller so a coincident entry pin's silhouette pokes out around the edges — the user can tell another pin is underneath
candidate styling distinct from Collection Entry pins (orange tint, smaller size) so the user can tell *result-to-adopt* from *already-saved*

altAffordances.label: Pick a provider candidate (add-to-collection mode)
altAffordances.appliesWhen: `collection-context` is set — the pin tap funnels straight into the collection picker, skipping LocationSheet

lists.composition: Drawn from `search-context.candidates`, the candidate list committed by COMMIT_SEARCH_TO_MAP and refreshed by SEARCH_THIS_AREA. The list is *only* the unadopted provider candidates from that committed set — existing-entry hits are already drawn by the `pins` list (their owning Entry's pin) and would double-render.
lists.emptyState: If a SEARCH_THIS_AREA refresh returns zero candidates, the searchResults mode stays active with an empty candidate set; the chip remains available for further re-queries and CLEAR_SEARCH exits the mode.

invariants.text: Typing into the `search` region while `search-context` is set fires `CLEAR_SEARCH`; editing the query never filters the committed candidate set.
The `commit-search-to-map` affordance renders only when at least one unadopted provider candidate is present in the dropdown; existing-entry-only results do not enable it.
invariants.note: Text-only — the precondition is candidate-set-shape (dropdown content), not a context key or mode. Awaits an `enabled(affordance-id)` or candidate-set atom extension.

invariants.text: In `addToCollection` mode the `settingsButton` and `collectionsButton` regions are suppressed; the user cannot bounce into `Settings` or `CollectionList` mid-flow.
The `searchThisAreaChip` region renders only when the live viewport has drifted past a threshold from `search-context.viewportAtQuery`.

The candidate-pin to `LocationDraftSheet` to `AddLocationToCollection` to `MapOverview` round-trip preserves `search-context.candidates` and `search-context.viewportAtQuery`; the user returns to the same pins and viewport, not a cleared map.
